statement: For an affine scheme $X$ and a quasi-coherent sheaf $F$, $H^q(X,F)=0$ for every $q>0$.

hypotheses.text: The scheme X is affine and F is a quasi-coherent sheaf.

conclusion: For an affine scheme $X$ and a quasi-coherent sheaf $F$, $H^q(X,F)=0$ for every $q>0$.

proofs.name: Standard proof
proofs.slogan: Resolve the sheaf on principal open covers.
proofs.scope: Full proof for [affine scheme](c:affine-scheme) and [quasi-coherent sheaf](c:is-quasicoherent). The proof covers all listed hypotheses and every degree in the conclusion.

roles.why: Affineness supplies principal open covers. Quasi-coherence identifies sections with module localizations.

steps.slogan: Resolve the sheaf on principal open covers.
steps.detail: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $F=\widetilde M$. A finite principal cover $D(f_i)$ has sections $M_{f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p}}$ on each intersection. The elements $f_i$ generate the unit ideal after suitable powers.

steps.slogan: Check exactness of the augmented complex.
steps.detail: Localize the augmented Čech complex at each $f_i$. The cover then contains the whole local spectrum, so insertion of index $i$ gives a contracting homotopy. These localizations detect zero modules because the $D(f_i)$ cover the spectrum.

steps.slogan: Compare the complex with sheaf cohomology.
steps.detail: Principal covers are cofinal among covers of every affine open, and their intersections are principal opens. The acyclic-basis criterion identifies the zero positive Čech groups with the derived functors $H^q(X,F)$. Thus all positive groups vanish.

concepts.c:affine-scheme: Principal affine covers have localization complexes whose exactness the proof tests.
concepts.c:is-quasicoherent: Quasi-coherence identifies sections on intersections with localizations of one module.

statement: A quasi-compact scheme $X$ is affine if $H^1(X,I)=0$ for every quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $I\subset O_X$.

hypotheses.text: The scheme X is quasi-compact and every quasi-coherent ideal sheaf on X has zero first cohomology.

conclusion: A quasi-compact scheme $X$ is affine if $H^1(X,I)=0$ for every quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $I\subset O_X$.

proofs.name: Standard proof
proofs.slogan: Separate each closed point from an affine complement.
proofs.scope: Full proof for [scheme](c:scheme) and [ideal](c:ideal). The proof covers all listed hypotheses and every degree in the conclusion.

roles.why: Quasi-compactness gives a finite principal cover. The vanishing hypothesis lifts sections through ideal quotients.

steps.slogan: Separate each closed point from an affine complement.
steps.detail: For a closed point $x$ in an affine open $U$, choose ideals of $X\setminus U$ and $(X\setminus U)\cup\{x\}$. Their quotient is the residue field at $x$. Zero first cohomology lifts its element $1$ to a global function $f$ with $x\in X_f\subset U$.

steps.slogan: Obtain a finite affine principal cover.
steps.detail: Each $X_f=D(f|_U)$ is affine. These opens contain all closed points. A nonempty closed complement in the quasi-compact space would have a closed point, so the opens cover $X$. Keep finitely many functions $f_1,\ldots,f_n$.

steps.slogan: Lift the unit through the relation sheaf.
steps.detail: The map $O_X^n\to O_X$ with entries $f_i$ is surjective on stalks. Its kernel has a finite filtration whose factors are quasi-coherent ideals. Long exact sequences give zero first cohomology of the kernel, so there are global $a_i$ with $\sum a_if_i=1$.

steps.slogan: Identify the scheme with its affine spectrum.
steps.detail: The principal opens $X_{f_i}$ are affine and their functions generate the unit ideal in $A=\Gamma(X,O_X)$. Localization identifies each with $\operatorname{Spec}A_{f_i}$. These identifications agree on intersections and glue to $X\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$.

concepts.c:scheme: Closed subschemes and affine principal neighborhoods support the scheme-to-spectrum identification.
concepts.c:ideal: The ideal quotient isolates a closed point, and the kernel filtration permits section lifts.

statement: If every finite intersection in an open cover $U$ of a scheme $X$ is affine, then $\check H^q(U,F)\cong H^q(X,F)$ for every quasi-coherent sheaf $F$ and every $q\ge0$.

hypotheses.text: The open sets cover X, all their finite intersections are affine, and F is quasi-coherent.

conclusion: If every finite intersection in an open cover $U$ of a scheme $X$ is affine, then $\check H^q(U,F)\cong H^q(X,F)$ for every quasi-coherent sheaf $F$ and every $q\ge0$.

proofs.name: Standard proof
proofs.slogan: Resolve the sheaf with an injective complex.
proofs.scope: Full proof for [quasi-coherent sheaf](c:is-quasicoherent) and [cohomology](c:cohomology). The proof covers all listed hypotheses and every degree in the conclusion.

roles.why: The cover resolves global sections. Affineness and quasi-coherence make every positive intersection-cohomology group zero.

steps.slogan: Resolve the sheaf with an injective complex.
steps.detail: Take an injective resolution $F\to J^\bullet$ and form the double complex of its Čech sections. The augmented Čech complex of each injective sheaf is exact, so one filtration computes $H^*(X,F)$.

steps.slogan: Remove positive cohomology on each intersection.
steps.detail: The other filtration has terms $\prod H^q(U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_p},F)$. Affine vanishing makes every row with $q>0$ zero. The row with $q=0$ is the Čech complex of $F$.

steps.slogan: Read the comparison from the surviving row.
steps.detail: Both filtrations compute the same total cohomology. Only the section row survives, so its degree-$q$ cohomology equals $H^q(X,F)$. The comparison respects multiplication by global functions.

concepts.c:is-quasicoherent: Quasi-coherence supplies vanishing on every affine intersection of the cover.
concepts.c:cohomology: The two filtrations identify derived global sections with the section row of the double complex.

statement: If a nonempty quasi-compact scheme $X$ has affine diagonal and a cover by $t$ affine opens, then $H^q(X,F)=0$ for every quasi-coherent sheaf $F$ and every $q\ge t$.

hypotheses.text: The scheme X is nonempty, its diagonal is affine, the cover has t finite affine members, and F is quasi-coherent.

conclusion: If a nonempty quasi-compact scheme $X$ has affine diagonal and a cover by $t$ affine opens, then $H^q(X,F)=0$ for every quasi-coherent sheaf $F$ and every $q\ge t$.

proofs.name: Standard proof
proofs.slogan: Check that every intersection is affine.
proofs.scope: Full proof for [affine scheme](c:affine-scheme) and [cohomology](c:cohomology). The proof covers all listed hypotheses and every degree in the conclusion.

roles.why: The affine diagonal makes all cover intersections affine. The finite number of members bounds the alternating complex. Quasi-coherence permits Čech comparison, and nonemptiness gives t at least 1.

steps.slogan: Check that every intersection is affine.
steps.detail: The intersection of two affine opens is the inverse image of their product under the affine diagonal. It is therefore affine. Repeat this argument for any finite intersection in the cover.

steps.slogan: Compute cohomology with the alternating complex.
steps.detail: Affine-cover Čech comparison computes the sheaf cohomology. The alternating degree-$p$ term uses strictly increasing lists of $p+1$ indices among $t$ members.

steps.slogan: Bound the length of the complex.
steps.detail: For $p\ge t$ there is no such list, so the complex term is zero. Its cohomology is zero in every degree $q\ge t$. The bound does not assert zero in degree $t-1$.

concepts.c:affine-scheme: The affine diagonal makes all multiple intersections of the finite cover affine.
concepts.c:cohomology: Cohomology of the alternating complex vanishes above its last nonzero term.

statement: For a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$ and a quasi-coherent sheaf $F$ on $X$, every $R^qf_*F$ is quasi-coherent on $S$.

hypotheses.text: The morphism f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and F is quasi-coherent.

conclusion: For a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$ and a quasi-coherent sheaf $F$ on $X$, every $R^qf_*F$ is quasi-coherent on $S$.

proofs.slogan: Work over an affine open of the base.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [quasi-coherent sheaf](c:is-quasicoherent) and [scheme](c:scheme). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: Quasi-compactness gives finite affine covers. Quasi-separatedness controls intersections for the induction on open sets. Quasi-coherence supplies affine acyclicity and closure under the exact sequence.

steps.slogan: Work over an affine open of the base.
steps.detail: Higher direct images commute with restriction to base opens. Quasi-coherence is local on the base. We can therefore assume $S$ affine and $X$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

steps.slogan: Verify the claim on an affine source.
steps.detail: For an affine open $U\subset X$, the map $U\to S$ is affine. Its degree-zero pushforward is quasi-coherent, and all positive higher direct images vanish by affine vanishing.

steps.slogan: Join the affine cases by the relative exact sequence.
steps.detail: For a union $U\cup V$, relative Mayer-Vietoris expresses each higher direct image as an extension of a kernel and a cokernel of the direct images on $U,V,U\cap V$. Quasi-coherent sheaves form an abelian category. The quasi-compact open induction principle completes the proof.

concepts.c:is-quasicoherent: Quasi-coherent kernels, cokernels, and extensions preserve the property in relative Mayer-Vietoris.
concepts.c:scheme: Quasi-compact scheme opens permit induction from affine pieces and their intersections.

statement: For a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$ and a filtered system of abelian Zariski sheaves $F_i$, $R^qf_*(\operatorname{colim}_iF_i)\cong\operatorname{colim}_iR^qf_*F_i$ for all $q\ge0$.

hypotheses.text: The morphism f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and the system of abelian sheaves is filtered.

conclusion: For a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$ and a filtered system of abelian Zariski sheaves $F_i$, $R^qf_*(\operatorname{colim}_iF_i)\cong\operatorname{colim}_iR^qf_*F_i$ for all $q\ge0$.

proofs.name: Published proof outline
proofs.slogan: Restrict to affine opens of the base.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [scheme](c:scheme) and [cohomology](c:cohomology). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: The finiteness conditions give a coherent affine basis. Filtered colimits are exact and commute with finite cover data.

steps.slogan: Restrict to affine opens of the base.
steps.detail: On an affine base open $V$, the source $f^{-1}V$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Its affine basis has quasi-compact intersections. This is the finiteness input of the cohomology-colimit theorem.

steps.slogan: Commute cohomology with the filtered colimit.
steps.detail: The published coherent-basis argument resolves the sheaves on finite affine refinements. Filtered colimits commute with the finite limits of cover data and are exact for abelian groups. It gives $H^q(f^{-1}V,\operatorname{colim}F_i)=\operatorname{colim}H^q(f^{-1}V,F_i)$. Cohomology Lemma 20.19.1 proves this affine-basis compatibility. Lemma 20.19.2 passes from it to higher direct images.

steps.slogan: Sheafify the local comparison maps.
steps.detail: The maps agree under restriction between affine opens. Sheafification gives the required comparison of higher direct images. This result concerns all abelian sheaves, not only quasi-coherent sheaves.

concepts.c:scheme: The affine basis of the quasi-separated scheme has the finite intersection data the theorem requires.
concepts.c:cohomology: Derived sections commute with filtered colimits by the cited coherent-basis theorem.

statement: For a ring $A$, $n\ge1$, and $d\in\mathbf Z$, $H^0(\mathbf P^n_A,O(d))=A[T_0,\ldots,T_n]_d$. The top group $H^n$ has basis the degree-$d$ Laurent monomials with every exponent negative. Every intermediate cohomology group vanishes.

hypotheses.text: The base A is a commutative ring, n is at least 1, and d is an integer.

conclusion: For a ring $A$, $n\ge1$, and $d\in\mathbf Z$, $H^0(\mathbf P^n_A,O(d))=A[T_0,\ldots,T_n]_d$. The top group $H^n$ has basis the degree-$d$ Laurent monomials with every exponent negative. Every intermediate cohomology group vanishes.

proofs.name: Standard proof
proofs.slogan: Split the standard complex into monomial weights.
proofs.scope: Full proof for [projective space](c:projective-space) and [cohomology](c:cohomology). The proof covers all listed hypotheses and every degree in the conclusion.

roles.why: The ring supplies coefficients. The dimension n and twist d determine the index length and the total exponent.

steps.slogan: Split the standard complex into monomial weights.
steps.detail: The standard affine charts and all intersections are affine. Čech comparison computes the groups. Each Laurent monomial of total degree $d$ defines a separate weight subcomplex preserved by the differential.

steps.slogan: Compute weights with no negative exponents.
steps.detail: When every exponent is nonnegative, the weight complex is the ordinary simplex complex. It contributes one copy of $A$ in degree zero and nothing in higher degrees.

steps.slogan: Compute weights with every exponent negative.
steps.detail: When every exponent of the weight is negative, the monomial occurs only on the intersection of all n+1 charts. The weight contributes one copy of A in degree n. There are no such monomials for d greater than -n-1.

steps.slogan: Contract every remaining weight complex.
steps.detail: If the negative-index set is nonempty and proper, choose an index outside it. Insertion of that index, with the Čech sign, defines a homotopy $hd+dh=1$. These complexes are acyclic. The direct sum of all weights gives the asserted formula.

concepts.c:projective-space: The standard projective charts determine which negative monomial exponents can occur.
concepts.c:cohomology: Čech cohomology splits into weight complexes that compute the zero and top groups.

statement: Let $X$ be proper over a Noetherian ring $A$, $L$ an ample line bundle, and $F$ a coherent sheaf. Then $H^q(X,F\otimes L^d)=0$ for all $q>0$ and all sufficiently large integers $d$.

hypotheses.text: The base A is Noetherian, X is proper over A, L is ample, and F is coherent.

conclusion: Let $X$ be proper over a Noetherian ring $A$, $L$ an ample line bundle, and $F$ a coherent sheaf. Then $H^q(X,F\otimes L^d)=0$ for all $q>0$ and all sufficiently large integers $d$.

proofs.name: Published proof outline
proofs.slogan: Pass to a very ample power of the bundle.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [ample line bundle](c:ample-sheaf) and [coherent sheaf](c:coherent-sheaf). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: Properness turns an ample projective immersion into a closed immersion. Coherence gives finite presentations and the Noetherian base controls their kernels.

steps.slogan: Pass to a very ample power of the bundle.
steps.detail: Choose $r>0$ and a closed immersion $i:X\to\mathbf P^n_A$ with $L^r=i^*O(1)$. Properness makes the immersion closed. Pushforward along $i$ preserves coherence and cohomology. The embedding inputs are Morphisms Lemmas 29.40.4 and 29.42.7.

steps.slogan: Prove vanishing on projective space.
steps.detail: A coherent sheaf on projective space admits a surjection from a finite sum of twists $O(-a_j)$ with coherent kernel. The explicit twist formula gives zero positive cohomology for large twists. Descending induction on cohomological degree, using the kernel sequence and the uniform dimension bound, gives vanishing for the sheaf. Stacks Lemma 30.14.1 carries out this projective-space argument.

steps.slogan: Treat all residue classes of the twist.
steps.detail: Apply projective-space vanishing to $i_*(F\otimes L^s)$ for $0\le s<r$. The projection formula handles twists $d=rm+s$. There are finitely many values of $s$, so one threshold works for every sufficiently large $d$.

concepts.c:ample-sheaf: An ample power gives the closed projective immersion used in the reduction.
concepts.c:coherent-sheaf: Coherent kernels permit induction on cohomological degree after finite presentations by twists.

statement: On a scheme $X$ proper over a Noetherian ring, a line bundle $L$ is ample if and only if every coherent sheaf $F$ has $H^q(X,F\otimes L^n)=0$ for all $q>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$.

hypotheses.text: The scheme X is proper over a Noetherian ring, and L is a line bundle on X.

conclusion: On a scheme $X$ proper over a Noetherian ring, a line bundle $L$ is ample if and only if every coherent sheaf $F$ has $H^q(X,F\otimes L^n)=0$ for all $q>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$.

proofs.name: Published proof outline
proofs.slogan: Establish vanishing in the ample case.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [ample line bundle](c:ample-sheaf) and [coherent sheaf](c:coherent-sheaf). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: Properness over the Noetherian base makes X Noetherian. A line bundle has exact tensor powers and an affine section criterion.

steps.slogan: Establish vanishing in the ample case.
steps.detail: If $L$ is ample, Serre vanishing gives the required threshold for each coherent sheaf $F$. This proves the forward implication with all positive degrees at once.

steps.slogan: Lift sections through ideal quotients.
steps.detail: For the reverse implication, apply the assumed vanishing to coherent ideal sheaves. A first-cohomology obstruction to a section lift disappears after a suitable twist. The section argument of Stacks Lemma 30.3.3 produces powers of $L$ whose nonzero loci form affine neighborhoods of every point.

steps.slogan: Identify the affine section basis.
steps.detail: The affine nonzero loci of sections of positive powers of $L$ form a basis for the topology. This is the section criterion for ampleness. The cited proof supplies the ideal-lift argument, rather than an assertion that arbitrary vanishing implies positivity.

steps.slogan: Combine the two directions of the criterion.
steps.detail: Serre vanishing proves the forward direction. The ideal-section criterion proves the reverse direction. Both hold under properness and the Noetherian base, so the asserted equivalence follows.

concepts.c:ample-sheaf: The affine section basis obtained from vanishing is the criterion for ampleness.
concepts.c:coherent-sheaf: Coherent ideals measure section-lift obstructions and test all positive twists.

statement: If $f:Y\to X$ is finite and surjective between schemes proper over a Noetherian ring, then a line bundle $L$ on $X$ is ample if and only if $f^*L$ is ample.

hypotheses.text: The schemes X and Y are proper over a Noetherian ring, f is finite and surjective, and L is a line bundle.

conclusion: If $f:Y\to X$ is finite and surjective between schemes proper over a Noetherian ring, then a line bundle $L$ on $X$ is ample if and only if $f^*L$ is ample.

proofs.name: Published proof outline
proofs.slogan: Pull an ample bundle to the finite cover.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [ample line bundle](c:ample-sheaf) and [line bundle](c:line-bundle). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: Finiteness preserves coherent pushforwards and removes higher direct images. Surjectivity reaches each generic point in the coherent devissage.

steps.slogan: Pull an ample bundle to the finite cover.
steps.detail: A finite morphism is affine, hence quasi-affine. Pullback along a quasi-affine morphism preserves an ample line bundle. This gives the forward implication.

steps.slogan: Define a vanishing property for coherent sheaves.
steps.detail: Assume $f^*L$ ample. For a coherent sheaf $G$ on $X$, require eventual vanishing of positive cohomology of $G\otimes L^n$. Exact sequences and finite sums preserve this property.

steps.slogan: Verify the property on generic support pieces.
steps.detail: For each integral closed support Z with generic point xi, Lemmas 30.13.1 and 30.13.2 provide a pushforward G=f_*F supported on Z with maximal-ideal annihilation at xi. If J_xi=O_X,xi, they identify JG with f_*(f^(-1)J F). The projection formula and ample vanishing on Y prove eventual vanishing for every such ideal modification.

steps.slogan: Descend the vanishing criterion to the base.
steps.detail: The devissage proves eventual vanishing for every coherent sheaf on $X$. The cohomological ampleness criterion therefore makes $L$ ample. Surjectivity is essential to supply a support piece over each component. Coherent devissage in Lemma 30.12.8 gives this implication.

steps.slogan: Combine pullback and descent of positivity.
steps.detail: The first step proves that ampleness pulls back. The last three steps prove that an ample pullback forces ampleness on X. These implications give the stated equivalence.

concepts.c:ample-sheaf: Ample pullback supplies eventual vanishing needed for coherent devissage on the target.
concepts.c:line-bundle: Line-bundle tensor powers are exact and obey the finite-map projection formula.

statement: For a closed immersion $i:Z\to X$ of Noetherian schemes with the same underlying topological space, a line bundle $L$ on $X$ is ample if and only if $i^*L$ is ample on $Z$.

hypotheses.text: The schemes are Noetherian, the closed immersion is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces, and L is a line bundle on X.

conclusion: For a closed immersion $i:Z\to X$ of Noetherian schemes with the same underlying topological space, a line bundle $L$ on $X$ is ample if and only if $i^*L$ is ample on $Z$.

proofs.name: Published proof outline
proofs.slogan: Reduce the thickening to square-zero steps.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [ample line bundle](c:ample-sheaf) and [ideal](c:ideal). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: The Noetherian hypothesis makes the defining ideal nilpotent with one uniform exponent. The topological condition identifies the section neighborhoods. Invertibility makes tensor with each power exact.

steps.slogan: Reduce the thickening to square-zero steps.
steps.detail: Let $I$ define $Z$. Its support condition and Noetherian finiteness give $I^N=0$. The intermediate schemes cut out by the powers of $I$ reduce the converse to a square-zero thickening.

steps.slogan: Lift suitable powers of ample sections.
steps.detail: For $I^2=0$, the sequence $0\to I\otimes L^n\to L^n\to i_*i^*L^n\to0$ measures the lift obstruction. On the affine nonzero locus of an ample section $s$ on $Z$, localization kills this obstruction. For large $e$, $s^e$ times the obstruction is zero, and the boundary derivation formula makes a power of s lift.

steps.slogan: Recover affine nonzero loci on the thickening.
steps.detail: The lifted section has the same nonzero locus topologically. A nilpotent thickening of an affine scheme is affine. These loci cover $X$ and form the section basis for ampleness. The forward implication follows by restriction of an ample bundle.

concepts.c:ample-sheaf: Ample sections on the reduction give affine neighborhoods whose powers lift through the thickening.
concepts.c:ideal: The nilpotent defining ideal supplies the square-zero filtration and section-lift obstruction.

statement: For a separated finite-type morphism $X\to S$ with $S$ Noetherian, there is a proper surjective map $X^\prime\to X$ that is an isomorphism over a dense open, with $X^\prime$ quasi-projective over $S$.

hypotheses.text: The base S is Noetherian and X to S is separated and of finite type.

conclusion: For a separated finite-type morphism $X\to S$ with $S$ Noetherian, there is a proper surjective map $X^\prime\to X$ that is an isomorphism over a dense open, with $X^\prime$ quasi-projective over $S$.

proofs.name: Published proof outline
proofs.slogan: Choose charts with one common dense open.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [proper morphism](c:is-proper) and [projective space](c:projective-space). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: Noetherian finiteness supplies finitely many components and charts. Separatedness makes local projection maps agree on their common dense open. Finite type supplies projective chart immersions, and scheme-theoretic density controls their agreement.

steps.slogan: Choose charts with one common dense open.
steps.detail: The published construction chooses finitely many affine opens meeting every generic point. Their intersection U is dense. Replace X by the scheme-theoretic closure of U if needed, which preserves surjectivity and the isomorphism over U.

steps.slogan: Close the common open in a projective product.
steps.detail: Embed each affine chart into a projective space over S, then take the closure of the diagonal copy of U in their product. The projections to the chart closures are proper.

steps.slogan: Glue the inverse images of the original charts.
steps.detail: The inverse images of the charts form an open subscheme X prime of the projective product. The projections agree on the scheme-theoretically dense U. Separatedness of X makes them agree on overlaps, so they define a morphism to X.

steps.slogan: Check properness and the dense isomorphism.
steps.detail: The inclusion V_i into pi^(-1)(U_i) is proper over U_i, so its image is closed. It contains the scheme-theoretically dense common open U, hence pi^(-1)(U_i)=V_i. The same argument gives pi^(-1)(U)=U. Properness is therefore local on the chart cover, and the image is closed and contains dense U. A Segre embedding makes X prime quasi-projective.

concepts.c:is-proper: Proper projections identify the chart preimages and make the glued modification proper.
concepts.c:projective-space: The product of projective spaces contains the common-open closure and admits a Segre embedding.

roles.why: Properness supports Chow modification and finiteness. The Noetherian condition makes coherent sheaves stable under kernels and quotients.

steps.slogan: Localize the question on the base.
steps.detail: Work on a Noetherian affine open of S. The proper finite-type source is Noetherian. Long exact sequences make coherence of all higher direct images a two-out-of-three property for coherent source sheaves.

steps.slogan: Produce a coherent sheaf on each integral support.
steps.detail: Chow modifies an integral closed support Z by a projective Z prime. Choose a line bundle ample for both the modification and the map to the base. A large power has zero positive direct images for both maps. Relative vanishing is Lemma 30.16.2, obtained by ample vanishing on affine base opens.

steps.slogan: Push the ample power to the support.
steps.detail: Its pushforward G on Z is generically of rank one. Leray and the two vanishings show that G has zero positive higher direct images to S and coherent degree-zero image, by the projective theorem. Projective coherence is Lemma 30.16.3.

steps.slogan: Complete coherent devissage on the source.
steps.detail: The coherent devissage theorem extends the direct-image property from these generic rank-one support sheaves to all coherent sheaves. The closed immersions of supports are affine, so they preserve the relevant cohomology. This gives all degrees of the claimed result.

concepts.c:is-proper: Properness supplies the Chow modification and makes its projective immersion closed.
concepts.c:coherent-sheaf: Coherent kernels and generic-support devissage extend finite direct images to every source sheaf.

statement: For $X$ proper over a Noetherian ring $A$, a coherent sheaf $F$, and an ideal $I\subset A$, the natural map $H^q(X,F)^\wedge_I\to\varprojlim_nH^q(X,F/I^nF)$ is an isomorphism of topological modules for every $q\ge0$.

hypotheses.text: The base A is Noetherian, X is proper over A, F is coherent, and I is an ideal of A.

conclusion: For $X$ proper over a Noetherian ring $A$, a coherent sheaf $F$, and an ideal $I\subset A$, the natural map $H^q(X,F)^\wedge_I\to\varprojlim_nH^q(X,F/I^nF)$ is an isomorphism of topological modules for every $q\ge0$.

proofs.name: Published proof outline
proofs.slogan: Control kernels and stable images by Artin-Rees.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [completion](c:completion) and [coherent sheaf](c:coherent-sheaf). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: Properness gives finite cohomology. Noetherian Artin-Rees estimates control the inverse systems for powers of I.

steps.slogan: Control kernels and stable images by Artin-Rees.
steps.detail: Proper coherence makes M=H^q(X,F) finite. Lemma 30.20.4 supplies the Mittag-Leffler stable images N_n and the Artin-Rees bounds I^n M contained in K_n contained in I^(n-c) M for n at least c. Here M_n=H^q(X,F/I^n F), N_n is the image of M, and K_n is its kernel.

steps.slogan: Replace the system by its stable images.
steps.detail: The Mittag-Leffler stabilization identifies $\varprojlim M_n$ with $\varprojlim N_n$, with their limit topologies. Each $N_n$ is the quotient $M/K_n$.

steps.slogan: Identify the two completion topologies.
steps.detail: The two kernel containments show that the $K_n$ filtration and the I-adic filtration are cofinal. Their inverse limits are the same completion. The comparison is therefore both an algebraic isomorphism and a homeomorphism.

concepts.c:completion: Cofinal kernel and ideal-power filtrations give the same completion and limit topology.
concepts.c:coherent-sheaf: Coherent proper cohomology is finite, and Artin-Rees controls its ideal-power quotients.

statement: If $f:X\to Y$ is proper, $Y$ locally Noetherian, and $\dim X_y=d$, then $(R^qf_*F)_y=0$ for every coherent sheaf $F$ and every $q>d$.

hypotheses.text: The base Y is locally Noetherian, f is proper, F is coherent, and the fiber at y has finite dimension d.

conclusion: If $f:X\to Y$ is proper, $Y$ locally Noetherian, and $\dim X_y=d$, then $(R^qf_*F)_y=0$ for every coherent sheaf $F$ and every $q>d$.

proofs.name: Published proof outline
proofs.slogan: Use the common topology of fiber thickenings.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [coherent sheaf](c:coherent-sheaf) and [completion](c:completion). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: The fiber dimension bounds cohomology on all its thickenings. Proper coherence gives a finite stalk to which Nakayama applies.

steps.slogan: Use the common topology of fiber thickenings.
steps.detail: The fiber is Noetherian. Every infinitesimal thickening at y has the same underlying topological space and dimension d. Grothendieck vanishing therefore gives zero cohomology in degree $q>d$ on each thickening. These thickenings lie over the local base at y. The stalk comparison is Lemma 30.20.7.

steps.slogan: Compute the completed direct-image stalk.
steps.detail: The stalk version of formal functions identifies the completion of $(R^qf_*F)_y$ with the limit of those zero groups. Its completion is therefore zero.

steps.slogan: Descend zero completion to the stalk.
steps.detail: Proper coherence makes the stalk a finite module over the Noetherian local ring $O_{Y,y}$. Zero completion implies its quotient by the maximal ideal is zero. Nakayama then makes the module itself zero.

concepts.c:coherent-sheaf: Coherence makes the direct-image stalk finite so Nakayama detects zero completion.
concepts.c:completion: Maximal-ideal completion identifies the stalk with the inverse limit of fiber-thickening cohomology.

statement: For a proper morphism $f:X\to Y$ with $Y$ Noetherian and a line bundle $L$, if $L|_{X_y}$ is ample, then $L$ is relatively ample above some open neighborhood of $y$.

hypotheses.text: The base Y is Noetherian, f is proper, L is a line bundle, and its restriction to the fiber at y is ample.

conclusion: For a proper morphism $f:X\to Y$ with $Y$ Noetherian and a line bundle $L$, if $L|_{X_y}$ is ample, then $L$ is relatively ample above some open neighborhood of $y$.

proofs.name: Published proof outline
proofs.slogan: Choose a projective map on the fiber.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [ample line bundle](c:ample-sheaf) and [proper morphism](c:is-proper). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: Fiber ampleness supplies a projective map. Properness lets a neighborhood of the fiber control a neighborhood on the base. Noetherianity supports the section-extension lemma and finite failure loci.

steps.slogan: Choose a projective map on the fiber.
steps.detail: Choose a sufficiently large power of the fiber bundle with sections that define a closed immersion into projective space. The fiber-lift lemma in the published proof extends these sections after an open restriction of Y. The section-lift input is Lemma 30.21.3.

steps.slogan: Extend the map to a base neighborhood.
steps.detail: The sections generate on the chosen fiber. Their failure locus is closed, and its image under the proper map is closed and misses y. Remove that image to obtain a map $\varphi:X\to\mathbf P^r_Y$ with $L^d=\varphi^*O(1)$.

steps.slogan: Make the extended map finite.
steps.detail: The proper map $\varphi$ has finite fibers above the projective fiber at y. The local finiteness theorem and properness of the projective target over Y permit a further base restriction on which $\varphi$ is finite. Finiteness near the fiber is Lemma 30.21.2.

steps.slogan: Pull the ample bundle through the finite map.
steps.detail: Pullback of $O(1)$ along the finite map is relatively ample. Thus $L^d$, and hence L, is relatively ample on the resulting neighborhood. The statement gives existence of a neighborhood, not a global conclusion.

concepts.c:ample-sheaf: Fiber ampleness supplies generating sections, and finite pullback preserves relative positivity.
concepts.c:is-proper: Properness makes the images of failure loci closed so a base neighborhood can exclude them.

statement: For $X$ proper over a Noetherian ring $A$ and a coherent sheaf $F$ flat over $A$, $R\Gamma(X,F)$ is perfect. For every $A\to B$, its derived tensor with $B$ equals $R\Gamma(X_B,F_B)$.

hypotheses.text: The base A is Noetherian, X is proper over A, and F is coherent and flat over A.

conclusion: For $X$ proper over a Noetherian ring $A$ and a coherent sheaf $F$ flat over $A$, $R\Gamma(X,F)$ is perfect. For every $A\to B$, its derived tensor with $B$ equals $R\Gamma(X_B,F_B)$.

proofs.name: Published proof outline
proofs.slogan: Construct a bounded flat Čech model.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [flat module](c:flat-module) and [coherent sheaf](c:coherent-sheaf). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: Flatness makes Čech terms flat. Proper coherence makes their cohomology finite. Noetherian finiteness converts finite Tor amplitude to perfection.

steps.slogan: Construct a bounded flat Čech model.
steps.detail: Take a finite affine cover of the separated source. Its alternating Čech complex K computes derived global sections and is bounded. Relative flatness of F makes its terms flat A-modules.

steps.slogan: Compare the model after every base extension.
steps.detail: Affine localization and tensor identify $K\otimes_A B$ with the Čech complex of $F_B$ on $X_B$. Since K is a bounded flat complex, ordinary tensor equals derived tensor.

steps.slogan: Prove finite Tor amplitude and coherence.
steps.detail: Proper coherence gives finite A-modules $H^q(K)$. To bound Tor amplitude against any A-module M, use the square-zero algebra $A\oplus M$. The same base-change model has a uniform bounded range of cohomology. Thus K is pseudo-coherent with finite Tor amplitude, and is perfect. The derived-algebra criteria are More on Algebra Lemmas 15.66.17 and 15.76.2.

steps.slogan: Combine perfection with the base-change model.
steps.detail: The bounded flat model gives the comparison for every A-algebra B. Its finite cohomology and finite Tor amplitude make it perfect. These are the two asserted conclusions for the same derived global-sections object.

concepts.c:flat-module: Flat modules make every bounded Čech term a valid model for derived tensor.
concepts.c:coherent-sheaf: Coherence and properness make cohomology modules finite, which supplies pseudo-coherence.

statement: Every proper morphism $f:X\to S$ factors as $X\xrightarrow g S′\xrightarrow\pi S$, where $S′=\operatorname{Spec}_S(f_*O_X)$, $\pi$ is integral, $g$ is proper with geometrically connected fibers, and $g_*O_X=O_{S′}$.

hypotheses.text: The map f from X to S is a proper morphism of schemes.

conclusion: Every proper morphism $f:X\to S$ factors as $X\xrightarrow g S′\xrightarrow\pi S$, where $S′=\operatorname{Spec}_S(f_*O_X)$, $\pi$ is integral, $g$ is proper with geometrically connected fibers, and $g_*O_X=O_{S′}$.

proofs.name: Published proof outline
proofs.slogan: Construct the relative spectrum of global functions.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [proper morphism](c:is-proper) and [scheme](c:scheme). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: Properness gives an integral relative algebra and controls idempotents on fibers after étale base extension. Lemma 37.53.1 also proves the nonemptiness of the fibers.

steps.slogan: Construct the relative spectrum of global functions.
steps.detail: The universally closed factorization lemma constructs $S′=\operatorname{Spec}_S(f_*O_X)$ and the natural map g. It proves that $\pi$ is integral and that $g_*O_X=O_{S′}$. The inherited finite-type and separated properties make g proper.

steps.slogan: Test connectedness after étale base extension.
steps.detail: Work on an affine S prime. Flat base change preserves the identity of global functions under affine étale extensions. To prove geometric connectedness it suffices to prove connectedness of fibers after all such pointed étale extensions.

steps.slogan: Exclude nontrivial idempotents on a fiber.
steps.detail: The proper idempotent-lift lemma lifts an idempotent of a fiber to the base after localization. Its image factors through the residue field, whose only idempotents are 0 and 1. A nonempty fiber with no nontrivial idempotent is connected. This proves geometric connectedness after the tests. The idempotent-lift input is Derived Categories of Schemes Lemma 36.32.7.

concepts.c:is-proper: Properness supports the integral factorization and the idempotent-lift argument for its fibers.
concepts.c:scheme: Relative spectra of scheme algebras give the intermediate base that records fiber decompositions.

statement: For a scheme $S$ and a positive integer $n$ invertible on $S$, the sequence $1\to\mu_n\to\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{u\mapsto u^n}\mathbf G_m\to1$ is exact on both the small and big étale sites.

hypotheses.text: The integer n is positive and invertible on the scheme S.

conclusion: For a scheme $S$ and a positive integer $n$ invertible on $S$, the sequence $1\to\mu_n\to\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{u\mapsto u^n}\mathbf G_m\to1$ is exact on both the small and big étale sites.

proofs.name: Standard proof
proofs.slogan: Identify the kernel of the power map.
proofs.scope: Full proof for [etale site](c:etale-site) and [scheme](c:scheme). The proof covers all listed hypotheses and every degree in the conclusion.

roles.why: Invertibility of n makes the root cover étale. Positivity supplies a finite free algebra of nonzero rank.

steps.slogan: Identify the kernel of the power map.
steps.detail: The sheaf $\mu_n$ consists by definition of units u with $u^n=1$. Its inclusion is injective and its image is exactly the kernel of the nth-power map.

steps.slogan: Construct a finite cover that adjoins a root.
steps.detail: For a unit a on an affine test scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A$, form $B=A[T]/(T^n-a)$. It is finite free of rank n, hence faithfully flat. The root T is a unit in B because its nth power is a unit.

steps.slogan: Verify that the cover is étale and surjective.
steps.detail: The derivative $nT^{n-1}$ is a unit in B. Thus $A\to B$ is standard étale and Spec B is a surjective étale cover. On this cover a is the nth power of T. These covers prove sheaf surjectivity on each étale site, including n equal to 1.

steps.slogan: Combine kernel identification with local surjectivity.
steps.detail: The kernel is mu_n by the first step. Every unit acquires an nth root on the surjective etale cover of the third step. Thus the power map has exactly this kernel and is locally surjective, which proves exactness.

concepts.c:etale-site: Etale covers turn a unit into a local power and establish sheaf surjectivity.
concepts.c:scheme: Affine root-cover schemes glue over each test scheme to produce the required covering.

statement: A universal homeomorphism $u:X_0\to X$ induces an equivalence of étale topoi. For every abelian étale sheaf $F$, pullback gives $H^q_{et}(X,F)\cong H^q_{et}(X_0,u^{-1}F)$ for every $q\ge0$.

hypotheses.text: The morphism u is a universal homeomorphism of schemes and F is an abelian sheaf on the etale site of X.

conclusion: A universal homeomorphism $u:X_0\to X$ induces an equivalence of étale topoi. For every abelian étale sheaf $F$, pullback gives $H^q_{et}(X,F)\cong H^q_{et}(X_0,u^{-1}F)$ for every $q\ge0$.

proofs.name: Published proof outline
proofs.slogan: Descend étale objects through the homeomorphism.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [etale cohomology](c:etale-cohomology) and [scheme](c:scheme). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: The universal homeomorphism gives effective equivalence of etale objects and preserves their covering families. Abelian coefficients permit the injective-resolution argument at step 3.

steps.slogan: Descend étale objects through the homeomorphism.
steps.detail: The published topological-invariance theorem shows that base change gives an equivalence between the categories of étale schemes over X and over $X_0$. This uses the integral, radicial, and surjective properties of u, rather than a homeomorphism of ordinary spaces alone. The object equivalence is Theorem 59.45.2.

steps.slogan: Transport the étale covering families.
steps.detail: Surjectivity of a family after base change is equivalent to surjectivity before base change because u is a universal homeomorphism. The category equivalence therefore preserves the étale topology and induces an equivalence of sheaf categories.

steps.slogan: Compare the derived section functors.
steps.detail: Under this equivalence, global sections agree and abelian injectives correspond. Apply the equivalence to an injective resolution of F. The cohomology of the section complexes is identical in every degree.

concepts.c:etale-cohomology: Etale cohomology uses injective resolutions transported by the equivalence of sheaf categories.
concepts.c:scheme: Base change of etale schemes preserves covers under the universal homeomorphism.

statement: If $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ strictly henselian local, then $\Gamma(S,F)=F_{\bar s}$ at its geometric closed point. Global sections are exact, so $H^q_{et}(S,F)=0$ for every abelian sheaf $F$ and $q>0$.

hypotheses.text: The ring R is henselian local with separably closed residue field, and F is an etale sheaf.

conclusion: If $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ strictly henselian local, then $\Gamma(S,F)=F_{\bar s}$ at its geometric closed point. Global sections are exact, so $H^q_{et}(S,F)=0$ for every abelian sheaf $F$ and $q>0$.

proofs.name: Standard proof
proofs.slogan: Split each pointed étale neighborhood.
proofs.scope: Full proof for [henselian local ring](c:henselian-local-ring) and [etale cohomology](c:etale-cohomology). The proof covers all listed hypotheses and every degree in the conclusion.

roles.why: Henselian lifting splits every pointed etale neighborhood. The separably closed residue field makes each residue extension at the point trivial.

steps.slogan: Split each pointed étale neighborhood.
steps.detail: Choose an affine neighborhood of the point in an étale S-scheme. The henselian étale splitting theorem gives an R-algebra decomposition $A=R\times A^\prime$ compatible with the geometric closed point. Thus the neighborhood has an S-section through that point.

steps.slogan: Identify sections with the closed stalk.
steps.detail: The identity neighborhood S is cofinal in the pointed neighborhood system because of these sections. The colimit that defines the geometric stalk therefore equals the sections on S. This holds for any sheaf of sets.

steps.slogan: Derive the vanishing from exactness.
steps.detail: For abelian sheaves, geometric stalks are exact functors. The identified section functor is therefore exact. Its positive derived functors vanish, which is exactly the stated étale-cohomology vanishing.

concepts.c:henselian-local-ring: Henselian splitting supplies a section through every pointed etale neighborhood.
concepts.c:etale-cohomology: Etale cohomology derives the section functor, which equals the exact geometric stalk functor here.

statement: For an affine scheme $X$ of characteristic $p>0$, $H^q_{et}(X,\mathbf Z/p)=0$ for every $q\ge2$.

hypotheses.text: The scheme X is affine and has prime characteristic p.

conclusion: For an affine scheme $X$ of characteristic $p>0$, $H^q_{et}(X,\mathbf Z/p)=0$ for every $q\ge2$.

proofs.name: Standard proof
proofs.slogan: Establish the Artin-Schreier exact sequence.
proofs.scope: Full proof for [characteristic](c:characteristic) and [etale cohomology](c:etale-cohomology). The proof covers all listed hypotheses and every degree in the conclusion.

roles.why: Characteristic p makes Frobenius additive and gives an etale Artin-Schreier root cover. Affineness makes the structure sheaf acyclic.

steps.slogan: Establish the Artin-Schreier exact sequence.
steps.detail: The map $F-1:O_X\to O_X$ sends t to $t^p-t$. Its kernel is the constant sheaf $\mathbf F_p$. For any local section a, the monic polynomial $T^p-T-a$ defines a finite free cover with derivative -1, so the map is surjective as an étale sheaf map.

steps.slogan: Compute the structure-sheaf cohomology.
steps.detail: Etale and Zariski cohomology agree for quasi-coherent modules. Since X is affine, the affine vanishing theorem gives $H^r_{et}(X,O_X)=0$ for every $r>0$. The quasi-coherent comparison is Theorem 59.22.4.

steps.slogan: Read the long exact sequence above degree one.
steps.detail: For $q\ge2$, the exact sequence places $H^q_{et}(X,\mathbf F_p)$ between the zero groups $H^{q-1}(X,O_X)$ and $H^q(X,O_X)$. It is therefore zero. Degree one need not vanish because the section map $F-1$ need not be surjective.

concepts.c:characteristic: Prime characteristic makes Frobenius additive and the Artin-Schreier derivative equal to minus one.
concepts.c:etale-cohomology: The long exact etale cohomology sequence transfers structure-sheaf acyclicity to constant p-torsion.

statement: For a smooth curve $X$ over an algebraically closed field, $H^q_{et}(X,\mathbf G_m)=0$ for every $q\ge2$.

hypotheses.text: The scheme X is a smooth curve over an algebraically closed field.

conclusion: For a smooth curve $X$ over an algebraically closed field, $H^q_{et}(X,\mathbf G_m)=0$ for every $q\ge2$.

proofs.name: Published proof outline
proofs.slogan: Write the units and divisors exact sequence.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [etale cohomology](c:etale-cohomology) and [algebraic curve](c:algebraic-curve). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: Smoothness supplies discrete valuations and locally principal divisors. Algebraic closure gives Tsen vanishing and acyclicity of closed points.

steps.slogan: Write the units and divisors exact sequence.
steps.detail: For the generic inclusion j and the closed point inclusions $i_x$, smoothness gives $0\to\mathbf G_m\to j_*\mathbf G_{m,\eta}\to\bigoplus_x i_{x*}\mathbf Z\to0$. The valuation map is locally surjective because divisors on a regular curve are locally principal.

steps.slogan: Prove acyclicity of generic units.
steps.detail: For each component, Lemma 59.67.12 (Tag 03RG) gives zero positive multiplicative cohomology for its function field and algebraic extensions, using Tsen. Lemma 59.68.2 (Tag 03RJ) computes the stalks and proves R^q j_*G_m=0. Lemma 59.68.3 (Tag 03RK) then uses Leray to prove acyclicity of generic units. Use the disjoint union of generic points for a disconnected smooth curve.

steps.slogan: Prove acyclicity of the divisor sheaf.
steps.detail: Each closed point has algebraically closed residue field, so its positive cohomology is zero. Finite direct image is exact. Filtered-colimit compatibility therefore gives zero positive cohomology of the direct sum of point sheaves. This is Lemma 59.68.4 (Tag 03RL).

steps.slogan: Read the long exact sequence in high degrees.
steps.detail: The exact sequence now places $H^q(X,\mathbf G_m)$ between zero groups for $q\ge2$. It therefore vanishes. The degree-one group is the Picard group, which need not be zero.

concepts.c:etale-cohomology: The etale cohomology sequence combines the independent generic-unit and divisor-sheaf vanishings.
concepts.c:algebraic-curve: A smooth algebraic curve has discrete valuations and locally principal divisors.

statement: In a cartesian square with $f:X\to S$ smooth, $g:T\to S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $Y=X\times_ST$, and projections $h:Y\to X$, $e:Y\to T$, the map $f^{-1}R^qg_*F\to R^qh_*e^{-1}F$ is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$ and an abelian étale sheaf $F$ on $T$ whose torsion element orders are invertible on $S$.

hypotheses.text: The square is cartesian, f is smooth, g is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and F has torsion stalks of orders invertible on S.

conclusion: In a cartesian square with $f:X\to S$ smooth, $g:T\to S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $Y=X\times_ST$, and projections $h:Y\to X$, $e:Y\to T$, the map $f^{-1}R^qg_*F\to R^qh_*e^{-1}F$ is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$ and an abelian étale sheaf $F$ on $T$ whose torsion element orders are invertible on $S$.

proofs.name: Published proof outline
proofs.slogan: Reduce to curve charts and bounded torsion.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [etale cohomology](c:etale-cohomology) and [torsion](c:torsion). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: Smoothness reduces the source to curve charts. Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of g permits colimits and induction on covers. Invertible orders permit the etale Galois-cover argument.

steps.slogan: Reduce to curve charts and bounded torsion.
steps.detail: Etale localization expresses a smooth morphism through affine-space charts. Composition reduces it to relative dimension one. Express F as the filtered colimit of its n-torsion parts, with n invertible on S. Higher direct images commute with these colimits. The colimit input is Lemma 59.51.7.

steps.slogan: Reduce the target and the degree.
steps.detail: Relative Mayer-Vietoris reduces T to affine pieces. Induction on q and an injective resolution reduce the task to zero higher direct images of a pulled-back injective n-torsion sheaf. Limit descent reduces the affine bases to finite type over $\mathbf Z[1/n]$. Noetherian limit descent uses Lemmas 59.51.8 and 59.51.9.

steps.slogan: Kill a generic class by an étale cover.
steps.detail: First reduce to smooth relative curves with geometrically connected fibers and a section. Lemma 59.89.1 kills a generic class after finite field extensions by an etale Galois cover split over that section, with order dividing a power of n. Fundamental Groups Lemma 58.31.8 extends that cover after finite normalization of the bases. Lemma 59.51.5 spreads generic vanishing to a nonempty open V of T.

steps.slogan: Complete the induction on the target dimension.
steps.detail: Injectivity gives a split embedding into j_*I|_V plus i_*I_prime for the closed complement Z. Induction in degrees below q gives the Leray injection from H^q(Y,j_prime_*e_V^(-1)I|_V) into H^q(Y_V,e_V^(-1)I|_V), so the open contribution is zero. The closed contribution dies locally by induction on dim Z, which is less than dim T. This kills the class and completes the comparison.

concepts.c:etale-cohomology: Etale cohomology in lower degrees gives the Leray injection for the open contribution.
concepts.c:torsion: Reduction to n-torsion permits injective sheaves of Z/n-modules with n invertible.

statement: For an affine finite-type scheme $X$ over a field $K$, its étale cohomological dimension satisfies $\operatorname{cd}(X)\le\dim X+\operatorname{cd}(K)$.

hypotheses.text: The scheme X is affine and of finite type over the field K, with etale cohomological dimension defined using torsion abelian sheaves.

conclusion: For an affine finite-type scheme $X$ over a field $K$, its étale cohomological dimension satisfies $\operatorname{cd}(X)\le\dim X+\operatorname{cd}(K)$.

proofs.slogan: Reduce by finite Noether normalization.
proofs.scope: Cited outline for [etale cohomology](c:etale-cohomology) and [scheme](c:scheme). The cited text supplies the lemmas and the long arguments named in the steps.

roles.why: Finite type allows Noether normalization. Affineness supplies the improved dimension bound. The field cohomological dimension controls the residue-field contributions.

steps.slogan: Reduce by finite Noether normalization.
steps.detail: A finite map from X to affine d-space exists for $d=\dim X$. Finite etale direct image has no positive derived functors, so Leray reduces the bound to arbitrary torsion sheaves on affine d-space. Dimension zero is the finite-map case. The finite-map vanishing is Proposition 59.55.2. If cd(K) is infinite, the inequality is automatic.

steps.slogan: Estimate the boundary of a relative projective line.
steps.detail: Embed affine d-space in P^1 times affine (d-1)-space. Lemma 59.95.5 embeds a field of cohomological dimension 1 into each relevant strict-local punctured algebra. That algebra is a filtered limit of lower-dimensional algebras over the field, so induction and Lemmas 59.95.2 and 59.95.4 bound R^q j_* supports by residue transcendence degree d-q. Lemma 59.74.5 and Theorem 59.51.3 convert the support decomposition to boundary cohomology bounds.

steps.slogan: Analyze the relative Leray page.
steps.detail: The projective-line projection has higher direct images only through degree two. The boundary projection is an isomorphism. Thus for $q>2$, the relative affine-line direct image has the boundary support bound. For q equal to 2, the generic stalk is zero by the curve case.

steps.slogan: Bound each total cohomological degree.
steps.detail: For q equal to 0 or 1, the induction on affine $(d-1)$-space gives the required bound. The sharper boundary estimate treats q at least 2. Every term with total degree greater than $d+\operatorname{cd}K$ vanishes, so the final Leray sequence proves the claim.

concepts.c:etale-cohomology: Torsion etale cohomology defines the dimension bound and its Leray terms.
concepts.c:scheme: Finite-type affine schemes admit the finite Noether normalization used in the induction.
